Rename an SDTM findings domain into the CTAS long-format vocabulary

Standardize_Domain.Rd

The single step that translates SDTM column names into the CTAS + ctasapp vocabulary and joins the standardised subject metadata (studyid, site, country) onto every row. Downstream Input_*() functions consume the resulting long frame and transform values without needing to know which SDTM domain fed them.

Usage

Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain,
  dfSubjects,
  strSubjectCol = "USUBJID",
  strTestCDCol,
  strTestCol,
  strValueCol,
  strVisitCol = "VISIT",
  strVisitNumCol = "VISITNUM",
  strLowCol = NULL,
  strHighCol = NULL,
  strCharCol = NULL,
  strCategory,
  strPrefix = ""
)

Arguments

dfDomain

data.frame Raw SDTM findings.

dfSubjects

data.frame Standardised subject table with subject_id, site, and optionally studyid, country, region.

strSubjectCol, strTestCDCol, strTestCol, strValueCol, strVisitCol, strVisitNumCol

character SDTM column names to translate.

strLowCol, strHighCol

character Reference-bound columns. NULL when the source has no ranges.

strCharCol

character Optional character result column (e.g. LBSTRESC). Fills original_category where strValueCol is NA, so qualitative results stay visible in ctasapp's source data. NULL by default.

strCategory

character Constant stamped onto parameter_category_1.

strPrefix

character Optional prefix applied to parameter_id (e.g. "NUM" -> "NUM_SYSBP"). Empty by default; parameter_category_2 always keeps the raw test code so ctasapp can stitch sibling metrics.

Value

data.frame in the CTAS long-format vocabulary. Includes the raw SDTM-derived columns (visit, visitnum, value, and low/high when supplied) alongside the CTAS-ready columns (parameter_category_2, parameter_category_3 = "numeric", timepoint_1_name, timepoint_rank, result, baseline) and the ctasapp untransformed source columns (original_value, lower, upper, original_category). No rows are dropped apart from subjects absent from dfSubjects, so the output can serve as the untransformed frame. visitnum and timepoint_rank are recalculated as a contiguous 1..N row_number() within each (subject_id, parameter_id) group, ordered by the source VISITNUM with VISIT as a tiebreaker – matching ctasapp's recalculate_timepoint_rank(). The default output is ready to feed straight into Analyze_CTAS(); use Transform_Range() or Transform_Missing() to overwrite result/parameter_category_3/parameter_id for those transforms.

Details

Reference-bound columns (strLowCol/strHighCol) are optional and only meaningful for range-carrying sources such as LB.

Examples

Standardize_Domain(
  dfDomain = data.frame(
    USUBJID = "S1", VSTESTCD = "SYSBP", VSTEST = "Systolic Blood Pressure",
    VSSTRESN = 120, VISIT = "WEEK 2", VISITNUM = 3
  ),
  dfSubjects = data.frame(
    studyid = "A", subject_id = "S1", site = "701", country = "USA"
  ),
  strTestCDCol = "VSTESTCD", strTestCol = "VSTEST", strValueCol = "VSSTRESN",
  strCategory = "Vital Signs"
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 21
#>   subject_id parameter_id parameter_name          parameter_category_1
#>   <chr>      <chr>        <chr>                   <chr>               
#> 1 S1         SYSBP        Systolic Blood Pressure Vital Signs         
#> # ℹ 17 more variables: parameter_category_2 <chr>, parameter_category_3 <chr>,
#> #   visit <chr>, visitnum <int>, timepoint_1_name <chr>,
#> #   timepoint_2_name <chr>, timepoint_rank <int>, value <dbl>, result <dbl>,
#> #   baseline <dbl>, original_value <dbl>, lower <dbl>, upper <dbl>,
#> #   original_category <chr>, studyid <chr>, site <chr>, country <chr>
